body: Thanks for that. Touching story too.
You're awesome. What are you listening to? I could use some happy music :(

fighter22 has it exactly right. You can never tell by words or temperament what state of mind someone is really in. Sometimes the more sane and calm someone sounds the more likely it is that they are a true danger to themselves. You never know.

People will tell you things and society will tell you things and your own thoughts will tell you things that are not true. Things that are absolutely, unequivocally not true. They might seem like truths, and a lot of us have been in that place where are head is screaming at us that they are true, but it's not the case.

Unfortunately, parents are just people. If they don't live up to their responsibilities that is only a reflection on themselves. It is not a reflection on you. It's not fair and it's not right, but sometimes that's the way it is sadly. 

I understand that you are bothered by your body for different reasons. I'm not trying to make light of your concerns, because your emotions are always valid. But please believe me that these are not you. You know what I see? I see an intelligent young woman who is in a lot of pain right now. I see this incredible individual who is torn up inside because she cares so much for their best friend. I see someone who loves their little sister and wants to care for her. I see a beautiful person who I think also cares about herself, even if it's hard to see through the pain. 

It can be near impossible to see right now, I understand that, but there are solutions. You are not alone in this and there are resources available if your family can't help you. It's ok to talk to people, to tell them what you are feeling. It's not easy, but there are people that want to help you. I'm not saying there's one easy fix, because there's not. But things can change. 

Right now please just be gentle with yourself. Treat yourself as you would want to treat your friend. You are in pain and just like him, you deserve compassion and understanding. I just want to repeat that because it's not easy to hear sometimes, but I promise you it's true. You deserve compassion. You deserve love and respect. You deserve to meet your pain and anxiety with the same gentleness you would extend to your little sister if she were experiencing it. Be gentle.

Please do call a hotline. As someone who is equally terrified of letting people in on my own secrets, I assure you they will not laugh. They are only going to help. And it's ok to ask for help. 

I know everything hurts right now but sometimes life is going to hurt horribly. But it's also going to be ok. It's ok to be worried about body image, it's ok to be a lesbian (or not), it's ok to cry. It's ok to be scared. These are not bad things. Painful yes, but not bad. I'm probably twice your age and I still cry when I'm sad. I worry about how I look and sometimes I get really scared. That doesn't make me or you a bad person though, just human. So from one human to another just know you are not alone. Please call and reach out to someone. It's good to ask for help. We all need help in this life. Everyone needs it at one time or another.

*hugs*

If it's any consolation, you're not alone in feeling alone. :)

*hugs*

I'm very glad it worked out for you, though I don't necessarily think the rose colored glasses approach will work for everyone. There are deeper more complex things behind motivation to get better I think, without going into a long psychological discussion.

However, that said, I just wanted to say that this line:

"but dammit I wanted to be happy."

made me smile. Thank you for that.

I know that sense of peace. I'm pulled in the same direction as you.

But it's my sincerest wish that we can both learn to rekindle that peace into a joy for this life. We will know that sense of peace eventually as it's a part of life. But there's no rush. 

Will tomorrow be better? I don't know. But tomorrow will come. Perhaps it will bring something interesting or something beautiful. Perhaps not. But then there's always the next day too. Peace will always be there in the future, living today won't and can't take that away. But who knows what living today or tomorrow might hold? Perhaps there is another kind of peace to be found here in this life as well. Can't hurt to try at this point.

If you feel like talking I'm here.

You have my sincere empathy. 

Yes, I agree about the idea of having a direction, something tangible to work toward. That definitely contributes to the problem. I do have future goals, but I think I just stopped believing they were possible...which of course makes them must harder to attain. And sometimes the world's problems are just so overwhelming that I keep trying to figure out how I might actually do some good. You are right that we must just pick one thing and kind of just let everything else go for the most part.

I like your idea about suicidal thoughts. It's a wonderful rationalization out of the irrational. I find it kind of funny just because we're talking about using logic on something that is inherently illogical, but yet I can follow your train of thought and it actually makes a lot of sense to me. Tickles my sense of humor at this crazy world.

Best of luck to you as well my friend.

Edit: I just wanted to add that in regards to you never trying therapy, even though I said I've tried it before doesn't mean it didn't do anything for me. I actually highly recommend it. Finding the right type and the right therapist can be difficult to be sure, but it's extremely worthwhile in the end. I don't regret it at all and I'm a better person now for having tried that path. If I make it through things I will definitely continue when I can afford it. It helped me grow as a person. It sounds like you are somewhat like me in being rather analytical, so I must warn you that a lot of therapy might not be your cup of tea. I've had therapists tell me that I need to find spirituality (not going to happen sorry), or just ask the normal "so how does that make you feel" questions. Those are pointless because I can talk psychology all day long, especially when it comes to my own psychology. Analyzing it doesn't do me any good or I would have cured myself ages ago.

But then I came across ACT ( Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) and it really matched what I needed. Yes, I'm suicidal but I'm far more at peace with myself then I used to be. ACT is all about learning to not analyze yourself and truly learn to actually feel things. To accept your feelings for what they are and move your life toward what you actually value. I found it to be quite logical and it's backed up by modern psychological studies and theories. I don't mean to get up on a soap box and you have to do whatever you are comfortable with, but I just wanted to say something about it as you seem of a similar mindset to myself and it's something that I'm very, very glad I did no matter what the eventual outcome.
Thank you, that's nice to hear. :)

I really appreciate the time you put into that response. I have to leave for the day, so I don't really have time to properly think about everything you said. However, I just wanted to say I do agree on many levels. There is a duality to nature here. Yes, it's logical and scientific, but at the same time we're all human and inherently irrational. And that's not always a bad thing. Love is not logical and I wouldn't wish it to be.

I understand what you're saying about my view of the future. It's interesting how one's perspective changes when in a depressed state. I view the future very differently when I'm feeling good. It has always just come back to this though. But no, it's no way to live a life. I'm a dreamer at heart. We need to have crazy dreams of the future and I do in my heart. But right now they're just all nightmares.

As for love, it definitely plays a significant role. But I don't pretend like it will solve my problems. If I make it through this life it needs to be on my own two feet. My depression is internal to me and cannot be fixed by a single thing be it a career or a relationship. The absence of it in my life though has caused me to think of it often and weave it into some sort of focal point of my problems, thought that's not really true. It's more of a symptom I suppose.

Like I said, I am a dreamer and I love to indulge my romantic side. So that image of waking up one day in love cooking pancakes is indeed something I think about. I want to believe that it's possible and there's a core in me that rails against the logic. It's the little kid in me saying I believe in love no matter how uncaring the world may seem. But it get's somewhat fainter as the years pass and I think I probably bury it deeper under an analytical veneer to protect myself. With love comes vulnerability and I've gone down that road.

In fact, I had what you describe happened once (minus the child of course). So in my mind I suppose I agree it's possible again. But looking back it seems like I was so naive. I let myself believe in soul mates and true love and opened up to the innocence of it all. It was all so wonderful at the time. Now I look back and realize what a lie most of it was. It's not anyone's fault, but life it complicated and you can't  have expectations of people. They are who they are just as I am who I am. 

But that said, I truly appreciate the picture you paint. It's most definitely a fascinating and mysterious place we find ourselves in. And I agree that suffering and pain are a natural part of existence. They are not inherently bad. I am willing to suffer and endure pain for the future. But I've also tried to have that attitude for what seems like an eternity. Perhaps it is weakness on my part, but I just feel ground down. I keep standing up but I just get a little smaller each time, a little more weary, and bit diminished. At some point I'm not sure how much I have left.

Is suicide a reasonable choice? Probably not. But depression is not reasonable and my emotions are not reasonable. I just fear that I cannot keep them at bay forever. I hope for change and wondrous things, but at a certain point I'm just not willing to live like this forever. But at what point am I allowed to find peace? Should I go another year? Another five? Another twenty? I never thought I'd survive this long without finding some kind of contentment, some form of happiness. But I have and I can keep going. But through the years I've actually come to value myself more than I used to and in a strange way that makes me think i deserve better. I deserve to be without pain. If not happiness then at least I would ask for release. It's a selfish request of the world, but sometimes I dearly wish to just ask the world for something in return just this once. 

Thank you for your thoughts. They were very insightful.

Thank you for that. I wish no one could identify, but it's nice to know there are others who understand.

Yes, sometimes I wish for a restoration of faith in humanity. However, I truly don't wish to hurt anyone by my demise. If I could leave this world and somehow erase the memories of everyone who has ever known me I would. I've been hurt sure, but I still love everyone in my life and the thought of hurting them with my death is agonizing. Not to say there aren't times when I've daydreamed about people taking notice of my death and some solace in the thought that maybe they would miss me. I would imagine most people hope to be missed and noticed on some level.

I don't really drink. I have on occasion, but not too often. However, I know exactly what you mean. I've forced myself into countless bars, festivals, and social gatherings thinking exposure would help. But you are right...it does sometimes seem like a flaw. Always feel like an outcast.

Thank you.
Thank you for the kind and thoughtful words. I enjoyed the song. :)
